the_count_check_the_command_demanded.instruction: Report the observed count; if it differs from 931, that is the finding — stop and name it, do not stamp what you see.

intended_property_established_before_cha.conclusion: HEAD names the commit the document DESCRIBES.
intended_property_established_before_cha.reasoning: Forced by the header's own shape, not assumed. (1) The snapshot DATE is carried separately on the same line, so HEAD would be redundant if it meant 'last substantive rewrite'. (2) The tests stamp carries its OWN sha ('931 as of `8bb0cbc`'), so HEAD is the document-level equivalent of a per-fact stamp rather than a different kind of thing. (3) Under the 'describes' reading the current state is a defect; under the 'rewrite boundary' reading it is merely odd. The command's own evidence line — 'a document whose HEAD predates its own newest stamp is internally incoherent' — only holds under (1).
intended_property_established_before_cha.action_taken: Set to this command's parent commit, 91d243c, per the command's instruction for that branch.

the_defect_measured.relation: 039cabe is an ANCESTOR of 8bb0cbc — verified with git merge-base --is-ancestor. The document claimed to describe a commit older than the commit whose test count it reported.
the_defect_measured.staleness: 32 commits had modified HANDOVER.md since 039cabe; 9 since 8bb0cbc.
the_defect_measured.why_existing_guards_passed: All three assert properties equally true of a stale stamp: not-a-placeholder, resolves, is-an-ancestor. B21's repair of the stamp regex was correct and could not reach this, because the regex was never the reason these passed.

the_guard.coherence: HEAD must be the newest sha the document stamps. Catches 039cabe beside 8bb0cbc exactly.
the_guard.freshness: At most 3 commits may have modified HANDOVER.md between the stamp and the commit under test. The bound cannot be 0 — the commit writing a stamp necessarily edits the document — and 3 allows that commit, a merge, and one concurrent edit. Not finely tuned: observed staleness was 32, an order of magnitude clear.
the_guard.what_it_does_not_catch: Stated in the docstring per convention 26. Uniformly and consistently stale stamps pass coherence; freshness only knows whether the document moved. Neither establishes that a stamp is CORRECT.

a_self_inflicted_exhibit.what: The coherence guard's first anti-vacuity assertion demanded a DIFFERING sha to prove it was not vacuous. A correctly maintained document stamps every fact at the same commit, so the guard failed on exactly the state it exists to certify — caught by the suite one run later.
a_self_inflicted_exhibit.fix: Non-vacuity belongs to the PATTERN finding stamps, not to the shas differing.
a_self_inflicted_exhibit.why_kept_in_the_record: A guard that fails on correct input is the same family as one that cannot fail at all, and B21 is the row for that family.

questions_for_advisor.question: The command's own question: is HEAD meant to name the described commit, or a snapshot boundary that moves only on substantive rewrites?
questions_for_advisor.answer: Concluded: the described commit, on the three-part reasoning above. Recorded as a conclusion with its argument rather than an assumption, so it can be overruled cheaply. If the other reading was intended, the freshness guard is wrong and should be deleted rather than loosened — a boundary that moves only on rewrites is not mechanically checkable, which the command itself observes.
